versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (34 FR 541, the issue of January 15, 1969) is the order itself: its number, Executive Order 11443, is printed in a displaced heading after the text, and it creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated January 13, 1969. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by February 12, 1969), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by February 12, 1969) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.
